request.content: You are a helpful assistant that translates programming worked examples into other natural languages, maintaining both technical accuracy and the original code formatting.

[[TASK-DEFINITION]]
You will be given a worked example. Your job is to translate the [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] according to the [[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]].

[[WORKED-EXAMPLE]]
[[PROGRAM-NAME]]
Concatenating Strings and Numbers (Case 1)

[[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]]
Construct a program that uses variables x, y, and z to print "Python was invented in 1989.".

[[SOURCE-CODE]]
[[LINE01]] #Step 1: Assign initial values to the variables x, y, and z
[[LINE02]] x = "Python was invented in "
[[LINE03]] y = 1989
[[LINE04]] z = "."
[[LINE05]] #Step 2: Print the text using the variables initialized above 
[[LINE06]] print(x + str(y) + z)

[[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]]
[[LINE02.EXPL1]] This statement sets variable x to the string "Python was invented in ".
[[LINE03.EXPL1]] This statement sets variable y to the integer 1989.
[[LINE04.EXPL1]] This statement sets variable z to the string ".".
[[LINE06.EXPL1]] This statement concatenates the content of variables x, y, and z to print the requested output. We concatenate the content of these variables using the + operator. Variables x and z have a string value and we can use the + operator to concatenate their content. Variable y, on the other hand, has an integer value and its value can be concatenated with strings only when it is explicitly converted to a string using the str function.
[[LINE06.EXPL2]] Note that the concatenating and printing are done in the same line. That is, we don't have to store the concatenated string to a new variable at first and then print it in the next line.
[[LINE06.EXPL3]] Note that the + operator creates a new string from the contents of its operands joined. This string will be printed by the print function and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

[[LINE-DISTRACTORS]]
[[DIST1.LC]] print(x + y + z)
[[DIST2.LC]] print(x + z + str(y))
[[DIST3.LC]] x + str(y) + z
[[DIST4.LC]] x + y + z

[[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]]
Translate the given worked example into Arabic. Be sure to specifically translate the sections labeled [[PROGRAM-NAME]], [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]], [[SOURCE-CODE]], [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]], and [[LINE-DISTRACTORS]]. In the [[SOURCE-CODE]] section, translate ONLY user-defined string-literals and comments; make sure they are ASCII-folded (i.e., remove any accents or non-ASCII characters). Preserve the original format and Do NOT add, remove, or change any content beyond translation.

[[PROGRAM-NAME]]
ربط السلاسل والأرقام (الحالة 1)

[[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]]
أنشئ برنامجا يستخدم المتغيرات x و y و z لطباعة "تم اختراع بايثون في 1989.".

[[SOURCE-CODE]]
[[LINE01]] #Khatwa 1: 3ayyen al-qiyam al-ibtidaia lilmutaghayyirat x, y, wa z
[[LINE02]] x = "Python tumma ikhtira3 fi "
[[LINE03]] y = 1989
[[LINE04]] z = "."
[[LINE05]] #Khatwa 2: Taba3 al-nass b-istikhdam al-mutaghayyirat allati tumma ta3yeenha
[[LINE06]] print(x + str(y) + z)

[[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]]
[[LINE02.EXPL1]] تقوم هذه العبارة بتعيين المتغير x إلى السلسلة "Python tumma ikhtira3 fi ".
[[LINE03.EXPL1]] تقوم هذه العبارة بتعيين المتغير y إلى العدد الصحيح 1989.
[[LINE04.EXPL1]] تقوم هذه العبارة بتعيين المتغير z إلى السلسلة ".".
[[LINE06.EXPL1]] تقوم هذه العبارة بربط محتويات المتغيرات x و y و z لطباعة الناتج المطلوب. نربط محتويات هذه المتغيرات باستخدام عامل +. المتغيران x و z قيمتهما من نوع سلسلة نصية ويمكننا استخدام عامل + لربط محتوياتهما. أما المتغير y فله قيمة عددية ولا يمكن ربط قيمته مع سلاسل نصية إلا بعد تحويله صراحةً إلى سلسلة باستخدام الدالة str.
[[LINE06.EXPL2]] لاحظ أن عملية الربط والطباعة تتمان في نفس السطر. أي أننا لسنا بحاجة لتخزين السلسلة المجمعة في متغير جديد ثم طباعتها في السطر التالي.
[[LINE06.EXPL3]] لاحظ أن عامل + ينشئ سلسلة جديدة من محتويات معامليه متصلة. هذه السلسلة ستُطبع بواسطة دالة print وتتبعه محرف نهاية السطر.

[[LINE-DISTRACTORS]]
[[DIST1.LC]] print(x + y + z)
[[DIST2.LC]] print(x + z + str(y))
[[DIST3.LC]] x + str(y) + z
[[DIST4.LC]] x + y + z
